claim.text: A parser-only nested /* */ comment branch allows a genuine untouched public-domain upstream Prolog program to execute directly in Rust and reproduce twelve live SWI ordered answers without changing 264 previously supported native CLI behaviors.
claim.scope: SWI-Prolog demo/likes.pl pinned to 111385b9; 12 queries tested with external SWI 9.0.4 ELF64; historical 264-case exact CLI parity and parser Rust tests on ELF64+i686; Rust 1.85.1.
assumptions: Source and license Git blobs match external upstream commit
Block delimiters have lexical-whitespace semantics outside quoted atoms
SWI-Prolog 9.0.4 is an independent executable witness on this subset
Two Rust build variants and historical source are frozen by SHA
forbidden_promotions: No new performance gain or time attribution
No retired Gen19 continuation policy revival

specification.intended_object: Add support for byte-oriented nested /* */ comment skipping to the existing finite Horn-clause Rust lexer, without changing parsers for ordinary terms or execution semantics.
invariants: Original 922-byte upstream source accepted directly, with source hashes preserved
Fixed 12 SWI reference ordered outputs matched by new Rust on original
Nested, Pldoc and ordinary blocks supported; unterminated block rejected at opening position
Quoted atoms containing literal /* */ preserved, bare slash remains unsupported
264 previously accepted Rust CLI cases exact output/exit/stderr parity on ELF64+i686
known_answer_cases: 12 documented and observed original likes.pl queries
One outer block and nested block parsing
Original Gen18 rejects block comment at byte 440
Unclosed nested comment has exact error at first slash

implementation.commit: Generation 25 parser-only branch based on merged Generation 24 fb9e05acd87e3fe71052e83ef38f26b9c12701d3; immutable released Gen18 901c8b58c12fbe8b79f70b0118f951f3ed2fcf21
implementation.environment: Rust 1.85.1 release native ELF64 and i686 ELF32 with feature tests; SWI-Prolog 9.0.4 ELF64; Python 3 standard library
implementation.live_entrypoint: syntax::tokenize after '%' comments before ordinary tokens, followed by parse_program/query/solve; original source in new CLI and SWI; derivative controls
implementation.representation: Depth-counting iterative lexer on bytes; exact CLI stdout/stderr/exit and ordered atom bindings

preregistration.prediction: New Rust accepts original likes.pl and returns all 12 SWI ordered outputs, while Gen18 rejects original, comment-only controls match, unit negatives remain rejected and 264 supported cases have exact parity per ABI.
preregistration.primary_metric: Typed tuple of 12 source-original independent SWI concordance and unchanged 264 strict historical cases per ABI, no timing.
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Deterministic finite case set, two native ABIs for historical regressions and ELF64 live SWI; external implementation witness but not independently authored study or statistical interval.
preregistration.kill_condition: Any original source hash mismatch, SWI vs new Rust mismatch, swallowed quoted comment, missing nested close accepted, unsupported slash accepted, historical output drift, or unavailable reference.
preregistration.stop_condition: No WAM, GC, source rewriting, unification changes or ownership heuristic to rescue a parser-only failure.
preregistration.promotion_rule: M only for direct upstream source acceptance and bounded SWI/264-case parity after final exact-head checks; broader language claims stay H.

result.observed: First Gen25 dual-ABI run passed: 12/12 direct unmodified upstream SWI ordered answers matched on ELF64, patched original equals patched and Gen18 comment-normalized controls; 264/264 previously supported strict Rust CLI outputs matched on ELF64 and i686; default/feature Rust unit tests passed. The initial YAML failure was syntax-only and corrected.
result.effect_size: 12/12 external ordered-query concordance; 264/264 historical differential per ABI; previous unmodified source parse failure at byte 440 now accepted by patched Rust; no timing metric.
result.uncertainty: One public-domain teaching program and 12 project-selected queries, independent SWI implementation only on ELF64, no human external review or full ISO/Unicode test coverage.
